introducer.title: agentHost: scope client customizations to session working directories

cases.mechanism: A debounce-only scheduler admitted overlapping full customization scans whenever refresh events were separated by more than 50 ms but scans took longer. Extra scans repeated discovery, extension-provider IPC and agent reads, queued redundant bundled-content traversals, and invalidated completed initial results, delaying the custom-agent picker and session claim until a newer scan completed without being superseded.
cases.symptom: During a startup customization-event burst on slow discovery or remote filesystems, completed initial scans could be discarded, delaying picker population and the session-claim critical path while redundant scan I/O accumulated. This is established by scheduling and call-path evidence, not a measured timing result.
cases.fixedBehavior: The added ThrottledDelayer construction serializes scans within each shared session-type/root-set scope and coalesces eligible pending refreshes into one follow-up. Replacing the sequence guard with a disposal guard allows the first completed scan to publish and settle initial resolution instead of waiting for a scan that survives overlapping refreshes. Existing per-authority bundle sequencing and per-bundler I/O limits remain intact; independent scopes remain independent.
cases.evidence: The deleted base line 157 constructs a plain Delayer with a 50 ms debounce. Delayer.trigger (async.ts:443-454) clears completionPromise before invoking the asynchronous task, so another event after the debounce can start another scan before the previous one finishes. Scope listeners include prompt changes, sync-provider changes, plugin and MCP observable changes, and skill-folder file changes. Each scan enumerates prompt locations once, then runs resolveCustomizationRefs and resolveLocalCustomAgents concurrently. Local/user listings perform filesystem discovery and extension listings invoke provider IPC; custom-agent resolution reads each enabled agent file. Bundling is already sequenced per authority and limits source file operations to 10 per bundler, but each extra scan still enqueues another content-read/hash traversal. The deleted sequence guard discards completed results if a later scan has begun, and initial resolution completes only for an accepted scan. ActiveClientEntry.claim awaits scope.whenResolved (agentHostSessionHandler.ts:1304), and ambient draft agents feed the picker (agentHostChatContribution.ts:415-417). The added test at agentHostClientTools.test.ts:288-349 holds a scan open while ten changes arrive 100 ms apart and establishes one scan during the burst, first-result publication, and two total scans. Blame identifies c14ff798a753dc8afcf8081ffe90a4763a9ee226 as introducing the old Delayer construction.
